text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a recurring tail-latency blip after we tightened coalesce jitter this morning. Looks correlated with a kernel variant flip and a KV eviction burst.

maria: can you paste the logs/trace? was this on canary or prod?

alex: canary cluster (dedicated-2). quick log snippet:```
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] batch_size=24 coalesce_delay=1.2ms chosen_kernel=fast-fp16
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] batch_size=96 coalesce_delay=0.0ms chosen_kernel=slow-int8
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] kv_evictions=120 stall_ms=47
```

kevin: ugh — that pattern screams alignment: microbatches drifting into the same phase so we get a big batch and the runtime picks the compatibility kernel which pulls weights/temps and slows everything. eviction spike probably from KV cache pressure when the big batch touches many contexts.

anya: hypothesis: reduced jitter caused phase-lockstep across arrival streams -> bursty coalescing. simple fix might be to reintroduce a tiny enqueue jitter or randomize token-budget deadlines per-request.

maria: agree. do we have perf profiles showing kernel load times vs batch size? alex?

alex: attached a flame snippet in the profiling job (summarized): `kernel_load_io` dominates at batch_size >= 64 and int8 fallback has ~3-4x latency compared to fast-fp16 for short sequences. KV hit-rate drops ~15% during the big batches.

kevin: two-pronged approach: 1) short-term experiment — add micro-splay jitter (0-1.5ms) at enqueue to break lockstep; 2) medium-term — make kernel selector prefer low-latency kernel for <100 tokens even if slightly suboptimal for throughput to avoid cold kernel loads.

anya: + add queue-side token-budget smoothing: don't let a single queue accumulate >X tokens in 2ms window, spill to next tick.

infra-bot: Deployment note: scheduled canary config roll at 12:00 UTC. Config name: `microphase-splay-v1`.

maria: quick config suggestion (for canary):```yaml
enqueue_jitter_ms: {min: 0.0, max: 1.5}
queue_token_cap_window_ms: 2
queue_token_cap: 512
kernel_selection_override: 
  prefer_low_latency_for_short_seq: true
  short_seq_threshold_tokens: 100
```

alex: testing locally now — will run 6h load with synthetic arrivals tuned to mimic user arrival skew. will collect KV metrics and kernel-load histograms.

kevin: if results look good, want to run a 1h canary on dedicated-2 then 30m on prod-1. keep fallback to previous config.

anya: metric checklist: p95/p99 latency (gen+queue), KV hit rate, kernel-switch count, cold-kernel-loads/sec, batch-size distribution, token-per-batch histogram.

maria: thanks. also capture per-model sequence-length distrib so selector tweak has context.

alex: plan posted in PR (link) and will attach perf graphs. assigning owners: alex (experiment run + graphs), kevin (selector change PR), anya (queue cap + smoothing), maria (canary orchestration).

kevin: ack. quick note — we should avoid long-term dependence on jitter; better to make selector robust to bursty batches. but jitter is a cheap mitigation. :thumbsup:

anya: agreed. I'll prototype the smoothing algorithm today. alex lmk if you want an env with higher KV capacity to test.

alex: please — spin up kv-rich canary; will re-run after lunch.

infra-bot: Canary instance `canary-dedicated-2-kvplus` created. link: https://infra.internal/canary/3001234567

maria: great. let's reconvene 3pm PT to review graphs. :calendar:

kevin: sounds good. thanks all.
